info.name: Query Item
info.description:
# Description The Query Item API is a simple query tool, to retrieve information about items and their locations within a store. ## Getting Started 1. Populate the collection variables with your Consumer Key (`clientId`) and Consumer Secret (`clientSecret`) 2. In the collection's Authorization section, use the *Get New Access Token* button to get an access token, then click *Use Token* so it can be used in subsequent requests. ## Environments We have three environments to help you develop your applications and safely interface with our APIs. You can use the three environments as part of your SDLC in progressing your application from sandbox, to test to our live APIs. Check the collection variables to set the correct `baseUrl` and `authenticationURL` to match the environment for your API keys. | **Environment** | **URLs** | | --- | --- | | **Sandbox** | AuthN URL: [https://connect.sandbox.api.bunnings.com.au/connect/token](https://connect.sandbox.api.bunnings.com.au/connect/token)

Base URL: [https://item.sandbox.api.bunnings.com.au/item](https://item.sandbox.api.bunnings.com.au/item) | | **Test** | AuthN URL: [https://authorisation-stg.api.bunnings.com.au/connect/token](https://authorisation-stg.api.bunnings.com.au/connect/token)

Base URL: [https://item.stg.api.bunnings.com.au/item](https://item.stg.api.bunnings.com.au/item) | | **Live** | AuthN URL: [https://authorisation.api.bunnings.com.au/connect/token](https://authorisation.api.bunnings.com.au/connect/token)

Base URL: [https://item.api.bunnings.com.au/item](https://item.api.bunnings.com.au/item) | ## Security Depending on the scope held, more or less functionality is available at an endpoint. There are further access controls in place to ensure the scope of the item inventory functionality is within a bounds suitable for the client making the request. ### itm:detail Get item details with restrictions based on access rights to the data. ## HATEOAS The Item API is built following the HATEOAS guidelines. When using the API, the client should start by first calling the `discovery` operation to get a list of possible links these links can then be followed to perform functions. If no correlation token is provided when using this service, it will generate a token for you in the header response. Contact Support: Name: Developer Support Email: [developer@bunnings.com.au](mailto:developer@bunnings.com.au)

query.description: Comma separated list of one or more of the Bunnings unique identifier for Items. This is a 7 digit numerical.

Select can optionally be used to project only the required properties of the entity/entities from the server.
- list required properties separated with a ','.
- property names are case insensitive.
- '\\*' can be used as a wild card for any property.
- use '/' to address complex type properties.

example: $select=name,address/state,contact/*/phoneNumber

Order By can be optionally used to control the sequence the entities of the collection are returned in.
This collection can have a maximum of 1 order properties separated by a ',' character.
Sorting can be done in asc or desc order by following the property name by a space and then the key words asc or desc.
If no direction is specified then asc is assumed.
This collection can be sorted by the following properties:
 - itemnumber
 - itemtype
example: $orderby=name desc,address/state asc.
default: itemnumber

(Required) Comma separated list of one or more store Identifiers
include item detail in the response

Select can optionally be used to project only the required properties of the entity/entities from the server.
- list required properties separated with a ','.
- property names are case insensitive.
- '\\*' can be used as a wild card for any property.
- use '/' to address complex type properties.

example: $select=name,address/state,contact/*/phoneNumber

variable.description: (Required) Country Code

request.description:
'Retrieves the ItemNumber, LocationCode, ItemStatus, IsOnRecall, IsRanged, PrimaryBarcode, InStoreLocations, Suppliers.'

NOTE-- Not more than 100 records are allowed as input and would result in an error.Calculation of total records is a product of itemNumbers and locationCodes.i.e total requests = LocationCodes * ItemNumbers For example if 10 item numbers are requested for 10 locationCodes, that makes the request = LocationCode * ItemNumbers = 100 total records.

So a query with total requests > 100 needs to be treated as a failure scenario and would result in a response with BAD REQUEST(Http Status code 400) With the reason as 'Too many records requested, the total number can't be more than 100 '.

NOTE-- Only the ItemNumbers found in the data source would be returned.So if 90 ItemNumbers are provided in the requests and only 89 are found in the data source, Only Details of 89 Items would be returned.

response.name: Success
